To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Roma adolescents report poorer self-rated health than non-Roma adolescents, but that the differences in health between the two groups are partly explained by socioeconomic status.

(i) the health of Roma adolescents is worse than that of non-Roma, (ii) the difference between Roma and non Roma is smaller when socioeconomic status is taken into account, (iii) the differences are smaller when social desirability is taken into account and (iv) there are no significant differences in mental health.
Roma adolescents living in eastern Slovakia reported poorer health than non-Roma, but that socioeconomic differences explain a large part of these differences.
